roads.name: North Drive
words: Curve after curve after curve: 31 in 3.3 miles, about 9 a mile.
The curves flow straight into one another.
From 13 to 18 ft, with 24 ft of up and down along the way.
roads.ratingNote: A full bar is top marks for that part; the percentages are each part's share of the rating. Curves, length and up and down are ranked against every road in the library. The rest are scored on the road itself: how few side roads join it, whether the curves or the limit set the pace, and how little is built up along it. At the 55 mph limit its corners still ask for about 0.96 g, so the curves, not the limit, set the pace. Most of it has no posted limit on the map, so this assumes 55 mph.

roads.name: Casey Key Road
words: Properly twisty: 23 curves in 3.5 miles, about 7 a mile.
Plenty of tight curves among them.
From 2 to 12 ft, with 56 ft of up and down along the way.
Homes line much of it: about 89 buildings a mile beside the road.

roads.name: Highway 70
words: Sweeping and steady: 15 curves in 4.0 miles.
The 3 miles at the west end are tamer, with about 3 side roads a mile.
Plenty of tight curves among them.
From 49 to 80 ft, with 43 ft of up and down along the way.
